restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224). Total work over all processors: T = 32,828,179,945,388 first-block C_32 trials at 1 unit plus 64 operations each, a hard counter cap of 400 T operations on all Step-2/3 work, 8 units of output verification, table build C = 2^38, starting solution D = 2^38 and characteristic search E = 32 * 593,858 CPU-s * 6,042,470 units per CPU-s = 2^46.7065 units; total 155,054,793,272,412 units = 2^47.1398.

Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes with M1 != M1'; complete SHA-256 with the standard IV, FIPS 180-4 padding, steps 0..31 on all three padded blocks, feed-forward and all 256 output bits; every output is recomputed before it is returned.

32-step truncation of the 35-step attack of Li, Liu, Wang and Shi (CRYPTO 2026, ePrint 2026/1080): its Fig. 6 characteristic, its 71 two-bit conditions under the stated readings and its starting solution as advice. The table and Step-2/3 specification follow hash-smash #26/#33 (winglock), restated in proof Sections 4-5.

One run with no restarts. Success probability >= 0.41069 from fresh independent first blocks, conditional on the declared rate heuristics, after subtracting a Chebyshev bound of 7.56e-6 on stopping at the counter cap. No certificate is supplied.

Measured inputs are credited public participant measurements (#296, #396, #26, #227), not runs made for this package: the matching rate q, the Step-2/3 stage pass rates, the table moments, the completed characteristic-search ledger and the callgrind CPU-second calibration. Our own checks (proof Section 14) are exact finite checks only. Our own measurements (proof Section 15) are a per-instruction costing of the x86-64 CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21 code and 17 CryptoMiniSat instruction-rate runs on SHA-256 CNF. They support the CPU-second price and do not re-run the charged search.

heuristics.statement: A first block M0 of fresh uniform words, compressed as CV1 = C_32(IV, M0), yields at least q = 2^-17.3583 expected valid tuples (records passing Step 2 tests (a)-(g)) against TAB2 of 1,396,774,912 records, and at most 2^-17.3166.
heuristics.scope: The exact P1-P4 sets and the Step-2 tests of proof Sections 4-5, with C_32 first blocks from the standard IV.
heuristics.extrapolation: Public participant measurement #296: four runs of 2^32 C_32 first blocks, one per index-part of TAB2, 25,936 valid tuples, pooled 2^-17.3373 with 99% interval [2^-17.3583, 2^-17.3166]. Corroborated by #26's runs (2^-17.3337), the #227 campaign counts (2^-17.326) and the analytic prediction 2^-17.3254. Extrapolated to T = 2^44.9 fresh trials.
heuristics.limitations: Credited participant runs, not organizer executions and not repeated for this package. CV1 words are treated as uniform for the Step-2 tests.

heuristics.statement: For a valid tuple, each of the 196,608 P4 entries passes Step-3 stages 16..31 with probability at least p = 2^-46, and at least one entry passes with probability r >= 2^-28.415 (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: Second-block steps 16..22 and schedule words W16..W31 under the Fig. 6 characteristic. Entries share W14 in 12 groups of 2^14; the shared W20 conditions are charged in the second moment.
heuristics.extrapolation: The condition count is 45 printed by S plus the unprinted E16[29] = E17[29] (#26). #296's cumulative stage rates over 2^32.248 candidates match the count through step 21 (2^-3.000, 2^-15.000, then 22, 5 and 1 survivors). The 13 W20/W22 carry conditions after step 21 are extrapolated. Both S's published tuple and the public 32-step pair of #227 pass every stage in our checks.
heuristics.limitations: Independence beyond the W14 grouping is assumed, not proved. One extra independent condition would lower the success bound to 0.31 at this T (proof Section 13).

heuristics.statement: For the number V of valid tuples in one trial, E[C(V,2)] <= q * 2^-5.
heuristics.scope: Valid tuples produced from one first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: #296 observed 9 within-part pairs in 2^34 part-trials and bounded the cross-part pairs from multiplicity sums. The charged 2^-5 exceeds that estimate by more than 20x.
heuristics.limitations: Cross-part pairs were not observed directly. This is a credited participant measurement.

heuristics.statement: Constructing the Fig. 6 characteristic by S's four-step SAT/SMT search, without S's intermediate outputs, costs at most 32 * 593,858 solver CPU-seconds on the measurement machine.
heuristics.scope: The one-time characteristic search, charged in preprocessing as E. Its memory is covered by search-peak-memory.
heuristics.extrapolation: #396 ran S's procedure with the authors' public model and STP 2.3.4 + CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21. Its 59 calls, all charged including timeouts and abandoned calls, used 593,858 CPU-s, and the run returned a characteristic whose signed rows equal Fig. 6. Because the run used S's nabla W and S's tA threshold, #396 priced a blind re-derivation from its own call ledger at 6.3-8.4 times that, and added a residual factor 4 for solver variance and model choice. The product 32 is adopted unchanged.
heuristics.limitations: S's own search time is unpublished. The factor 32 is argued from a measured ledger, not executed. tE4 = 76 was reached but not proved optimal. Doubling the factor raises the total to 2^47.939.

heuristics.statement: One solver CPU-second on the measurement machine costs at most kappa = 6,042,470 target-compression units (2^22.527 units, 2^33.646 primitive word operations). This is 12.29 operations per retired instruction at the calibrated 2^30.026 instructions per CPU-second.
heuristics.scope: The STP + CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21 calls priced in E and D, on the machine that ran them. No price is claimed for any other machine.
heuristics.extrapolation: kappa = ceil(R_cal * m_class * S / C). R_cal: callgrind calibration (#296/#396), 44,197,378,388 instructions in 40.42 native CPU-s (repeats 41.07 and 41.10), i.e. 2^30.026 per CPU-s, from one single-threaded call. m_class = 6.6432: the measured opcode mix priced at 5 per instruction, and at 400 for the 0.416% divide/multiply/floating-point share. S = 1.85: our 14 single-thread CryptoMiniSat runs on SHA-256 CNF (9 instance shapes, 1-3 seeds, up to 281 CPU-s) varied in instructions per CPU-s by at most 1.842 (max/min) on one machine. Long runs, larger resident sets and 4 threads lowered the rate or left it unchanged (0.84-1.00x). Reserve: our per-form costing of the x86-64 CryptoMiniSat 5.11.21 code gives 1.71 operations per ordinary instruction in the hot functions and 1.73 over the library, so m_static = 3.388. kappa therefore covers charged calls retiring up to 3.63 times R_cal (proof Section 15).
heuristics.limitations: The instruction rate of the 59 charged calls was not measured. It is assumed to be within 1.85x of the one calibrated call under the class pricing, or 3.63x under the per-form costing. Our rate runs used another machine, instruction set and solver build (Apple M4 Pro, arm64, CryptoMiniSat 5.16.0); they enter only as a relative spread, and their absolute rate (2^32.6-2^33.5) is not used. The per-form costing is static, not a dynamic profile, and the wheel build may differ from the STP-linked library. No organizer experiment can re-measure the rate. kappa = 2^23, as in our earlier package, gives 47.504.

heuristics.statement: Producing the Step-1 starting solution (the advice words A4..A13, E8..E13, W12, W13) costs at most 2^38 units.
heuristics.scope: One SAT solution of the characteristic through step 13, charged once as D.
heuristics.extrapolation: S reports about 2^34.3, with no unit; read as 35-step compressions this is below 2^34.46 units. #296's two exact-value-model runs of the same task took 908.8 CPU-s in total, which gives 2^37.36 units at the kappa of cpu-second-pricing with a factor 32 (2^37.83 at kappa = 2^23). D = 2^38 covers both readings.
heuristics.limitations: S's unit and trace are unpublished. D is below 0.3% of the total, so this does not change the claimed exponent at two decimals.

heuristics.statement: The per-trial counted Step-2/3 operations X satisfy E[X] <= 238.94 and E[X^2] <= 6.436e12 under the charges of proof Section 5.4.
heuristics.scope: Only the probability of stopping at the counter cap of 400 T. The time bound itself is a hard cap and does not depend on this.
heuristics.extrapolation: Inputs are the exact occupancy mean N/2^27, the measured maximum bucket of 936, the multiplicity sum 5.758e9 (Cauchy-Schwarz over 4 parts), the Step-2 cumulative pass fractions bounded by 0.51, 1/15, 1/120 and 1/240, the Step-3 stage-16/17 pass fractions bounded by 2^-2.99 and 2^-14.9, and q at its upper limit. The quantities come from #296. Chebyshev then gives a cap-stop probability <= 7.56e-6.
heuristics.limitations: Credited measurements. Even a 100x larger second moment keeps the cap-stop term below 0.001, which leaves the success bound above 0.40.

heuristics.statement: The characteristic and starting-solution searches need at most 2^33 bytes of memory at their peak.
heuristics.scope: Memory only. The searches run before the attack phase.
heuristics.extrapolation: #296 and #396 measured a peak resident set of 5.25 GiB over all calls. It is added to the attack memory anyway: 28,661,817,348 bytes = 2^34.739.
heuristics.limitations: S's own search memory is not reported. Memory does not affect the score.
